posts.name: Ronway
posts.cooked:
Just wanted to say that I love Sentinels of the Multiverse. Within the first week I was playing it up to five times a day. Have became quite fond of Ra, Tempest, Absolute Zero and Bunker, not sute which one is quite my favorite since each one has their unique playing style. All the heroes also have a uniqueness to them but just haven’t got my attention yet. And then the villians, the first few times against Baron Blade I was beginning to think of him as a chump but then he got the right cards at the right time and it sure showed me not to under estimate him anymore. Citizen Dawn and Grand Warlord Voss are probably the toughest individuals to go up against, only beating Voss a total of twice and Dawn once. Omnitron too is a force to be reakoned with when him playing two cards each round, inless of course no components or drones have made their way to the trash. Haven’t had a chance to try out the advanced rules yet, mostly can only get enough for a group of three and that provides enough difficulties as is.And teamwork is a necessity after I played a few solo games and found out it does make it easier building strategies using all heroes rather then working solo. Now just have to transfer that into when playing with others. The quotes from the “comics” are also a very nice touch, adding more personality to the characters.

All in all, incredible game and totally pumped to see some expansions. Maybe the hippo costumed guy from Haka’s “Savage Mana” card? Or maybe it will be the lacky of the possible nemesis of Haka? I guess only time will tell, hopefully long before December 2012 so I can have some time to enjoy it.

Edit: Decided to throw in a poll to see some of people’s favorite hero to play as or backstory wise if they can’t think decide.

Agreed Jodie, considering that everytime I have beaten Baron Blade’s first side after nine turns shows if it was on advanced it would of been doubled that meaning I would of been way past the 15 limit. Also playing Tempest or Absolute Zero using “Electrical Storm” or “Cold Snap”, then “Elemental Redstributor” comes into play and all of a sudden the heroes begin to slowly drop in HP, throw “Backlash Field” on top of that and it makes it even worse. I just got lucky my first two times playing it and those two cards were never drawn. Heck, I didn’t even see “Blade Battalion” until my fourth time playing.

posts.name: Kat
posts.cooked:
Currently Voss is causing more trouble for me than Citizen Dawn… We’ve been playing with 3 players rather than 4 which completely ups the difficulty level. Even so, it is frustratingly fun and is making me want to defeat him even more!

I also love how easy it is to get involved with the game… like I said, Voss has been kicking our butts so we’ve created a story line involving the environments. He conquered Mars first, then landed on the planet in the jungle (little did he expect dinosaurs, but dealt with them accordingly), slowly making his way toward the city.

Brilliant Game!

posts.name: Ronway
posts.cooked: Played a game against Voss two days ago using Haka, Legacy, and Visionary. Got him all the way down to nineteen HP before he ended up pulling a victory against us. What got us was “Forced Deployment” being played and their were sixteen minions in the trash. Visionary was able to put half back into the bottom of the deck, but that left her with only two HP so when Villian’s turn came around she was sadly eliminated on the spot. Haka went on the next turn, and Legacy on the following turn. What a sad shame it was, that night we fought all four villians and didn’t achieve one victory.

posts.name: beevolant
posts.cooked:
Forced Deployment is the worst in the late game. I’ve found that your only hope is that the first turn player has something that can blow up ongoing cards so that you get a round to kill some of the minions before they get a chance to hit you.

I’ve only beat Citizen Dawn once on advanced mode, but that was with 6 players (we decided 6 against advanced Dawn would be more fun than two games of 3), and we beat her… barely. At the end of the game only The Wraith was alive (and only because every turn at least one incapacitated player had her play her innate power of reduce the next two damage (which stacks!), and she had fewer than 5 hit points. Awesome.
